newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kyrgyz police seize 218 kg of raw opium.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyz police seize 218 kg of raw opium.

text.p: Police in Kyrgyzstan have seized 218 kg (480 lb) of raw opium worth about $2 million, the biggest haul since the former Soviet republic gained independence in 1991, the interior ministry said on Thursday.
Interior ministry officials, quoted by Interfax news agency, said the drugs were discovered in a car in the country's southern Osh region after a routine police inspection.
Kyrgyzstan, a poor country which borders China and Tajikstan, has called for international aid to battle the explosion in the narcotics trade following the Soviet Union's collapse.

The remote, mountainous country has found itself on the opium trail, with drugs from war-torn Afghanistan crossing Tajikistan, itself torn apart by an Islamic insurgency, across its poorly guarded southern frontier. The drugs then travel north through Kazakhstan and to Europe via Russia and Ukraine.

The commander of Russian border guards in Kyrgyzstan, Pavel Vasco, told Interfax that drugs seizures along the Kyrgyz-Tajik border had doubled this year from 1995. He said his troops had so far seized over a tonne of narcotics in 1996.
